questions.question: What are numbered block parameters in Ruby?
questions.title: Numbered Block Parameters
questions.direct_answer: Numbered parameters (Ruby 2.7+) let you skip declaring block params: `[1,2,3].each { puts _1 }` — _1 is the first block argument, _2 the second, etc. No `|x|` needed. Useful for tiny blocks where a name adds no clarity: `words.map { _1.upcase }`, `sum = nums.reduce(0) { _1 + _2 }` (_1 is the accumulator, _2 the element). They're a shorthand — for readability or more than ~2 params, declare named params (|x, y|). _1 is the same as declaring |x|; mixing _1 and named params in the same block is an error. They work in any block (each/map/reduce/times). They're purely syntactic sugar — the block is still a closure. Use them for one-liners; named params for anything with logic or more args.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know numbered parameters (Ruby 2.7+) — _1, _2, ... in blocks without declaring params.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Mixing _1 and named params (error), or overusing them for complex blocks (hurts readability).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Numbered block params (Ruby 2.7+): _1, _2 in blocks without |x|. Shorthand for tiny blocks. reduce: _1 + _2. Don't mix with named params.

sections.title: Skip the Params
sections.content: Numbered parameters (Ruby 2.7 plus) let you skip declaring block params: 1 2 3 dot each block puts _1 — _1 is the first block argument, _2 the second, etc. No pipe x pipe needed. Useful for tiny blocks where a name adds no clarity: words dot map block _1 dot upcase, sum nums reduce 0 block _1 plus _2 (_1 is the accumulator, _2 the element). They're a shorthand — for readability or more than ~2 params, declare named params (pipe x y pipe). _1 is the same as declaring pipe x pipe; mixing _1 and named params in the same block is an error. They work in any block (each/map/reduce/times). They're purely syntactic sugar — the block is still a closure. Use them for one-liners; named params for anything with logic or more args.

sections.title: Numbered Params
sections.content:
_1, _2 in blocks (no |x|). Shorthand. reduce: _1 + _2. Don't mix with named params.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  B[block { puts _1 }] --> P[_1 = first arg]
  R[reduce { _1 + _2 }] --> A[_1 acc, _2 elem]
  M[mix _1 and |x|] --> E[error]
```

sections.title: Numbered block parameters
sections.content:
```ruby
# Ruby 2.7+: numbered block parameters (_1, _2, ...)
# No need to declare |x|:
[1, 2, 3].each { puts _1 }       # 1 2 3
words = %w[hi bye]
words.map { _1.upcase }          # ['HI', 'BYE']

# _1 = first arg, _2 = second, etc.
%w[a b].each_with_index { puts "#{_1} #{_2}" }  # a 0 / b 1

# In reduce: _1 is the accumulator, _2 the element
sum = [1, 2, 3].reduce(0) { _1 + _2 }   # 6
# (same as: reduce(0) { |acc, n| acc + n })

# Equivalent to declaring params:
[1,2,3].map { |x| x * 2 }   ==  [1,2,3].map { _1 * 2 }   # true

# DON'T mix _1 and named params in the same block (error):
# [1,2].map { |x| _1 }        # SyntaxError

# Works in any block (each/map/reduce/times/select):
3.times { puts _1 }            # 0 1 2
[1,2,3].select { _1.even? }   # [2]

# Use for ONE-LINERS; named params for logic or many args.
# Purely syntactic sugar; the block is still a closure.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Mixing _1 and named params in the same block (SyntaxError).
Overusing them for complex blocks (hurts readability — use named params).
Forgetting _1 in reduce is the accumulator (not the element).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Numbered parameters (Ruby 2.7+): _1, _2 in blocks without declaring |x|.
_1 is the first block arg, _2 the second; works in any block.
In reduce, _1 is the accumulator, _2 the element.
Don't mix _1 and named params in the same block (SyntaxError).
Use for one-liners; named params for logic or more than ~2 args (readability).
